name: Latent
long_description:
Latent is a control layer for AI, built on interpretability. It reads signals inside a model as it works and checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds. Then it lets the output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached.

Reading the model is far cheaper than running a second LLM, so it can check every step. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge.

It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or in your own cloud, and calibrates to your traffic with every review.
one_liner: Stop AI agent mistakes by reading the model’s mind

launches.body:
Hey everyone! I'm [Vedant Gaur](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vedantgaur/) from [Latent](https://runlatent.ai/).

**TL;DR: Latent stops AI agent mistakes and wrong answers before they land. It reads signals inside the model while it works, checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds, and stops the ones about to go wrong. It works with any model and costs over 600x less than an LLM judge.**

Website: [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai)\
Start free: [app.runlatent.ai](http://app.runlatent.ai)

[Demo](https://youtu.be/Dd8cez0CIDY)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123748&key=user_uploads/1788540/af18344d-59fb-4a63-9f84-65e38f95a216)

**The Problem:**

AI fails quietly. A model gives a confident answer that’s wrong, like the wrong dosage or a refund policy that doesn’t exist. An agent takes a shortcut it was told not to take. The dashboard is green and last week’s evals passed. You find out when a customer does.

The usual fix is a second LLM that re-reads every output. That’s slow and expensive, so most teams check a sample, and everything else ships unchecked. As agents run longer with no one watching, that gap gets wider.

Every payment gets a fraud check before it clears. As agents take on more of the work, every AI decision will need one too.

**What We're Doing:**

**1. Reading the model while it works**\
Latent scores every answer and agent step from signals inside the model. On self-hosted models it adds no latency. On API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, a lightweight reader scores each answer in milliseconds.

**2. Acting before anyone is affected**\
You decide what happens: let it through, hold it and show a fallback, re-ask a stronger model, or send it to review with the reason attached. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge checking every step.

**3. Checking every answer instead of a sample**\
Our classifier costs over 600x less than an LLM judge, so you can run it on all of your traffic. That catches 4x more hallucinations than checking a sample.

**4. Getting sharper on your data**\
Every answer your team confirms or clears becomes a label, so Latent calibrates to your traffic and improves the more you use it.

**5. Making models better, not just safer**\
Send only the riskiest answers to a stronger model, and a small model gets close to frontier accuracy. On financial Q&A, routing the riskiest half to a frontier model lands within 2 points of it at 60% of the cost.

**6. Fitting into your stack**\
_pip install runlatent_ wraps the model calls you already make, or you can point traffic at our OpenAI-compatible gateway. Self-hosted models run it as a vLLM plugin. Use it hosted, or run everything in your own cloud with nothing leaving your environment.

**The team:**

At Penn (M&T), I published interpretability research at ACL and EMNLP, plus NeurIPS workshop work, on what a model’s internals reveal that its outputs don’t. Latent is the production version of that work. Before this, I worked on post-training at Amazon and Robinhood.

**Asks:**

If this sounds like your stack, I'd love to work with you. Reach out if you're:

* Running long-running agents, where one bad step early can derail everything after it.
* Doing research or continual learning, and want a signal the moment a model starts going wrong.
* Shipping AI in healthcare, finance, insurance, legal, or anywhere else a wrong answer is expensive.
* Paying for LLM judges or human review and want to cut that bill.

Intros help too. If you know someone leading AI at a company in one of those industries, I'd be grateful for a connection.

Email me at [vedant@runlatent.ai](mailto:vedant@runlatent.ai), or book time at [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai).
